title: Meiji 1874: three Army telegrams on the end of the Taiwan expedition, army 1-7 coordinate square (telegrams 1-2 first deciphered by Ohno 2010, re-read; telegram 3 read in part)

system.summary: Iroha 7x7 Polybius square (row, column digits 1-7), voicing marks as separate cells

prior_solution.where: Ohno Tetsuya 大野哲弥, 「明治7年の陸軍省暗号の制定：佐賀の乱後の陸軍暗号電報利用状況」, 情報化社会・メディア研究 7 (2010) 37-44: describes the cipher and deciphers telegrams 1 (his no. 4031 = C04025783900) and 2 (no. 4027 = C04025783500), not C10071951300. The cipher is also described by Nagata Junko 長田順行, 『西南の役と暗号』 (1989) p. 170, and by Satoshi Tomokiyo, Cryptiana, meijiarmy.htm (2014; table meijiarmy1). Our own check of 28 Oct 2026 (web JA/EN, NDL column, this repository) missed them; Satoshi Tomokiyo pointed them out on 29 Oct and 10 Nov 2026.

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout chose the documents and set the rules (protocol and key frozen before a held-out check); AI agents transcribed, read, checked and wrote up; doubtful signs were settled by Brice Dudout's targeted visual reviews (shapes only, no plaintext shown). Satoshi Tomokiyo pointed out the prior work (29 Oct and 10 Nov 2026).
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: Protocol hypothesis H1 (traditional iroha square, row-column) read the telegram directly.

Frozen key on held-out telegram 2 (C04025783500, 63 pairs): 0 of 200 permuted control keys reach it (trigram score and lexicon). The key was later found to be already published (Nagata 1989, Ohno 2010, Tomokiyo 2014).

outcome.method_basis: The key is the army's 1-7 coordinate square of 1874, already described by Nagata (1989), Ohno (2010) and Tomokiyo (2014, meijiarmy1). We re-found it independently as an a-priori hypothesis (28 Oct 2026) before knowing these works, and do not claim it. Telegrams 1-2 were first deciphered by Ohno (2010); telegram 3 is read here for the first time, to our knowledge.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Daniel's rule, certain + probable words, restored not counted: telegram 1 20/20, telegram 2 27/29, telegram 3 18/23; 65/72 = 90.3%.

texts.label: Army Ministry telegram, 8 Nov 1874
texts.summary: The China negotiations ended peacefully; China agreed to pay an indemnity (Taiwan expedition, Beijing agreement of 31 Oct 1874). First deciphered by Ohno (2010, no. 4031); re-read here.

reading_review.note: read as Japanese sentences, 20/20 words; independent re-reading of Ohno 2010 no. 4031

texts.label: Army Ministry telegram, 8 Nov 1874 (break-off rumour denied)
texts.summary: Newspapers report that the China negotiations have broken down, but the government has no word; sure news will follow; give no credence to rumours. 27/29 words certain or probable. First deciphered by Ohno (2010, no. 4027); continuation also read by Satoshi Tomokiyo.

reading_review.note: read as sentences, 27/29 words certain or probable; cursive 2/3 digits settled by plates C02, C03, C09 (Brice Dudout, shapes only); independent re-reading of Ohno 2010 no. 4027

texts.label: Major Onuma, Nagasaki, 22 Oct 1874 (relaying consul Shinagawa)
texts.summary: Letter from Beijing: Okubo ... the Chinese must answer by the 20th; then he will probably withdraw. 18/23 words certain or probable (22/23 with restored words that depend on two declared clerk corrections). Not in Ohno 2010.

reading_review.note: read as sentences in the cipher part, 18/23 words certain or probable; digit runs segmented with plates C05, C07 (Brice Dudout); two declared clerk corrections; first reading to our knowledge
